Trustworthy Evaluation of AI-Assisted Painting Restoration

SDXL Inpainting

Evaluation status: partial_evaluation. This report summarizes validated Notebook 09–30 evidence and creates no new scientific evidence.

Executive Summary

This standalone report evaluates SDXL Inpainting using validated restoration, metric, robustness, uncertainty, failure, explanation, and compute evidence.

Evaluation statuspartial_evaluationBounded partial scope
Paintings1924 cases
Candidates2424 with explanation-catalog coverage
First-place anchors0/11sdxl_four_model_subset
Mean runtime199.519 sRecorded local system
Flagged candidates24/24At least one triggered trustworthiness flag
Thesis alignment: RQ1, RQ2 and RQ3: quality, conditional behaviour and bounded human-review support.

What the evidence shows

  • Evaluation status: partial_evaluation.
  • Coverage: 19 paintings, 24 cases and 24 candidates.
Conclusion: SDXL produced technically valid results for its bounded 35-case branch. Its complete-population position remains inconclusive because it was not evaluated across the full controlled population.
Limitation: Visual plausibility is not equivalent to historical or restoration trustworthiness. Better or worse metric-defined outcomes do not establish historical correctness. Any unsupported implication remains inconclusive.

1. Method Identity

This section defines what the evaluated method is, what role it can reasonably serve, and where that role ends.

Field Value
Model family Prompt Conditioned Sdxl Latent Diffusion Inpainting
Methodological role Bounded Higher Capacity Diffusion Candidate
Implementation Diffusers StableDiffusionXLInpaintPipeline
Model identifier diffusers/stable-diffusion-xl-1.0-inpainting-0.1
Deterministic False
Prompt dependent True
Execution device cuda
Precision float16

Intended uses

  • bounded partial comparison
  • local compute and memory feasibility evidence
  • transparent SDXL scaling projection

Excluded uses

  • full controlled-dataset ranking
  • universal comparison against the three full-scope methods
  • historically verified reconstruction or conservation approval
Thesis alignment: RQ3: establishes the method's role inside a human-centred workflow.

What the evidence shows

  • Methodological role: bounded higher capacity diffusion candidate.
  • Strengths: higher-capacity diffusion lineage; technically valid 768px partial outputs; direct local feasibility evidence.
  • Weaknesses: only 35 purposively selected cases, of which 24 completed; very high runtime on recorded hardware; no repeated-seed uncertainty coverage.
Conclusion: SDXL Inpainting should be interpreted within its declared methodological role rather than as an autonomous restoration authority.
Limitation: Visual plausibility is not equivalent to historical or restoration trustworthiness. Better or worse metric-defined outcomes do not establish historical correctness. Any unsupported implication remains inconclusive.

3. Overall Quality Evidence

Eleven transparent quality anchors combine classical, perceptual, feature, spatial, local, semantic, and structural evidence. Lower plotted rank is better.

Thesis alignment: RQ1: compares restoration quality using complementary evidence.

What the evidence shows

  • First-place transparent quality anchors: 0 of 11.
  • No complete-scope family-balanced rank was assigned to SDXL.
Conclusion: SDXL produced technically valid results for its bounded 35-case branch. Its complete-population position remains inconclusive because it was not evaluated across the full controlled population.
Limitation: Visual plausibility is not equivalent to historical or restoration trustworthiness. Better or worse metric-defined outcomes do not establish historical correctness. Any unsupported implication remains inconclusive.

4. Damage Types and Experiments

This section keeps damage-size sensitivity, mask robustness, and synthetic-degradation evidence separate. Positive adverse slopes indicate worse restoration behaviour under the stated exposure.

Thesis alignment: RQ2: evaluates damage size, mask geometry and synthetic degradation.

What the evidence shows

  • Damage-size sensitivity and mask-robustness extensions were not evaluated for SDXL.
  • Its bounded branch contains 24 completed candidates.
Conclusion: SDXL damage sensitivity remains inconclusive. Its bounded evidence supports feasibility inspection rather than complete-population comparison.
Limitation: Focused experiments use controlled 35-painting cohorts. Metric-native slope magnitudes are not directly interchangeable.

5. Texture, Colour, and Seam Behaviour

Local texture, colour, and seam diagnostics test whether a plausible-looking repair remains visibly inconsistent near or inside the restored region.

Thesis alignment: RQ1: evaluates localized defects missed by global similarity.

What the evidence shows

  • First-place local anchors: 0 of three.
  • The anchors cover texture error, masked colour difference and boundary-seam mismatch.
Conclusion: SDXL Inpainting ranked first on 0 of the three local evidence anchors.
Limitation: Texture, colour and seam measurements represent different failure modes and use different scales.

6. Semantic and Structural Evidence

Semantic and structural measurements test local content and organization beyond pixel similarity. They remain proxies rather than proof of historical meaning.

Thesis alignment: RQ1 and the semantic/XAI extension: evaluates local structure and feature agreement.

What the evidence shows

  • First-place semantic or structural anchors: 0 of three.
  • Evidence covers local DINO similarity, structural affinity and structural SSIM.
Conclusion: SDXL Inpainting ranked first on 0 of the three semantic and structural anchors.
Limitation: Feature agreement does not establish iconographic correctness, artist intent or historical truth.

7. Uncertainty, Prompt, and Stability Evidence

Uncertainty is treated as empirical repeated-seed variability only. Deterministic methods and insufficient seed coverage are reported as not applicable.

Thesis alignment: RQ2: distinguishes stochastic sensitivity from restoration quality.

What the evidence shows

  • Only one SDXL seed was executed for each completed bounded case.
  • Repeated-seed uncertainty was therefore not assigned.
Conclusion: SDXL uncertainty remains inconclusive because repeated-seed evidence is absent.
Limitation: Empirical disagreement is not calibrated confidence and does not measure historical correctness.

What the evidence shows

12. Decision Support

Strengths

  • higher-capacity diffusion lineage
  • technically valid 768px partial outputs
  • direct local feasibility evidence

Weaknesses

  • only 35 purposively selected cases, of which 24 completed
  • very high runtime on recorded hardware
  • no repeated-seed uncertainty coverage
Thesis alignment: RQ3: translates evidence into bounded human-review support.

What the evidence shows

  • Intended uses: bounded partial comparison; local compute and memory feasibility evidence; transparent SDXL scaling projection.
  • Main strengths: higher-capacity diffusion lineage; technically valid 768px partial outputs; direct local feasibility evidence.
  • Main weaknesses: only 35 purposively selected cases, of which 24 completed; very high runtime on recorded hardware; no repeated-seed uncertainty coverage.
Conclusion: SDXL Inpainting is best used within its declared role and with comparison against references, diagnostics, flags and human judgement.
Limitation: The report supports prioritization and inspection; it does not authorize physical conservation treatment.

13. Limitations

The limitations below are retained from the canonical model card and evidence contract.

  • Runtime and memory observations describe one recorded local workstation and software environment.
  • The controlled 300-painting values are executed observations; only the explicitly labelled 600-painting and full-design SDXL values are projections.
  • Projected storage covers notebook-owned output artifacts and excludes model caches, environments, Git history, and downstream metric outputs.
  • SDXL scheduled 35 bounded cases across 30 paintings; 24 completed, one timed out and ten were skipped under the declared budget, so it cannot support a full-scope ranking.
  • LaMa per-case runtime includes transparent allocation from IOPaint batch wall-clock measurements.
  • Quality-anchor wins are descriptive validated Notebook 21 evidence, not a universal quality or conservation score.
  • The 35 cases are a predeclared balanced purposive scope and do not represent a full SDXL evaluation.
  • The 35 case observations span 30 paintings; repeated cases from five retained pilot anchors are nested observations.
  • A timeout or CUDA out-of-memory failure is hardware/runtime evidence and must not be interpreted as poor restoration quality.
  • Only technically validated completed candidates may enter downstream metric computation.
  • The global seven-hour budget can leave later scheduled cases explicitly unexecuted.
  • SDXL outputs are plausible prompt-conditioned inpaintings, not historically verified reconstructions or conservation recommendations.
Thesis alignment: RQ1, RQ2 and RQ3: defines what the evaluation does and does not establish.

What the evidence shows

  • Excluded uses: full controlled-dataset ranking; universal comparison against the three full-scope methods; historically verified reconstruction or conservation approval.
  • 12 persisted limitations are retained from the model card.
Conclusion: The evidence identifies comparatively better and worse metric-defined behaviour. Historical authenticity and physical conservation suitability remain inconclusive.
Limitation: Visual plausibility is not equivalent to historical or restoration trustworthiness. Better or worse metric-defined outcomes do not establish historical correctness. Any unsupported implication remains inconclusive.
